ruling_3_convergence_or_thrashing.answer: THRASHING. Not «it depends», not «converging with residue». Thrashing — and round 24 already ruled it, named the exit, saw the exit land, and watched the shape reappear one layer up within two rounds.
ruling_3_convergence_or_thrashing.the_count: FIVE commits in ninety minutes, five deployed, and every one of them closed the previous one's defect while introducing a new one of the same family. 5f38d56: the button contract missed the model's own emission site. f9a51f0: canonicalTitle rewrote «لا أريد العرض التجاري» into its affirmative, and the widened wantsInfo re-opened the founder's complaint #1 («التفاصيل والسعر لو سمحتم» short-circuiting to a brochure). 1cf9b6d: clean (dashboard only). e4121fa: the no-body branch returned a string starting «أُرسل», which the outer loop reads as proof a bubble was sent — silence, the exact failure the never-silence fallback exists to prevent; and a particle denylist that 10 of 11 verb-form Arabic refusals walked straight through. 7ee7756: «لا» and «موافق» added as BUTTON_INTENT keys next to a brand-new unprovenanced write path to the lead ledger.
ruling_3_convergence_or_thrashing.the_single_shape: Every one of these is the same move: WIDEN A SHARED TABLE OR MATCHER FOR ONE CONSUMER, RE-TEST ONLY THAT CONSUMER. BUTTON_INTENT, canonicalTitle's affix set, and wantsInfo's phrase set each have several readers. The tests are written per-reader, by whoever was in the file that hour. Round 24 diagnosed this precisely — «one string answering two opposed questions» — and named the exit: split `disclosed` from `asked`. That exit LANDED at round 25 (agent.ts:228-230, both derivations present, correctly commented). And the shape immediately reappeared one layer above the ladder, in `wantsInfo`, and then one layer above that, in `buttonIntent`. Fixing an instance of a structural defect by hand buys you exactly one round.
ruling_3_convergence_or_thrashing.why_i_am_not_calling_it_convergence: There is a real convergence case and I want to state it fairly before rejecting it: the per-defect code footprint IS shrinking, the mechanism changes ARE getting better (denylist→allowlist is a genuine inversion, not a patch — 0 of 14 named refusals invert, I measured it), and the gate grew 82→118→133 assertions. If severity were tracking size, this would be convergence. It is not. SEVERITY WENT UP ON THE LAST STEP. e4121fa's worst case was a wrong word on a button — visible, embarrassing, recoverable. 7ee7756's worst case is a SILENT, PERMANENT, FALSE WRITE to the lead ledger with a FABRICATED PROVENANCE STRING. «ضغط زر: لا» asserts a button press that never happened. This project has spent four rounds — Rule 2, Rule 4, Rule 7 — establishing that the system's own claims about itself must be true. The last commit of the round shipped a lie into the database. A process whose defects are getting smaller in bytes and larger in consequence is not converging on anything I would sign.
ruling_3_convergence_or_thrashing.the_second_tell: The instrument stopped discriminating. 133 green assertions, and the reviewer proved by mutation that flipping the real wantsInfo predicate from && to || leaves all 133 green. `assertButtonsHandled()` only checks emitted→has-intent, so ADDING a BUTTON_INTENT key is certified for free — which is exactly how «لا» and «موافق» walked in past a boot-time contract whose entire purpose is to stop unhandled button strings. When the gate's failure mode is silence on the change you actually made, the green number is not evidence, it is comfort.
the_exit_named_concretely: 1. PROVENANCE, NOT STRING EQUALITY. `buttonIntent()` must be unreachable for typed text. The distinction already exists on the wire — gupshup.ts parses msgType at both webhook versions — and was dropped at the call site. Gate every intent lookup on a real tap. (Note: this is exactly what is sitting UNCOMMITTED in the worktree right now — `isButtonTap()` at gupshup.ts:174 wired at index.ts:46. The exit has been found. It must land, be reviewed, and be deployed, because until it is, the defect is live.)

2. MAKE THE TABLE DECLARE ITS CONSUMERS. BUTTON_INTENT has at least four readers today: assertButtonsHandled, canonicalTitle, tappedCommercial, and the new decline→setOutcome writer. Adding one key is silently a change to all four. The check must assert, for every key, the behaviour of EVERY consumer — a consumer matrix, not a key list. This is the only change that converts «a new key is free» into «a new key costs N assertions», and it is the only thing that stops this class rather than its current instance.

3. ASSERTIONS EXECUTE THE SHIPPED EXPRESSION, NEVER RESTATE IT. MUT5 is proof: the gate slices `wantsInfo` out of agent.ts and hand-types the composition back. Extract `wantsInfo` to a named exported function and import it. A gate that reconstructs a predicate is a Rule 7 violation by construction, and this one is now being quoted upward as proof.

4. DO NOT DEPLOY A FIX BEFORE THE FIX IS REVIEWED. Five deploys, ninety minutes, four of them carrying an unreviewed new defect to production. His standing instruction is «once done, just deploy it and fly» — «once done» is load-bearing in that sentence, and this round treated it as «once written».

4. AND THE ONE THAT WOULD ACTUALLY MAKE HIM ANGRY, IF HE FOUND IT. The agent asks «هل تستخدمون حاليًا نظام HIS أو ERP؟» — its own prescribed question. grill.evidence: This is a genuine fit, not a bolt-on, and it earns the clean. The picker lives inside step ٣ of the existing wizard and inherits its card/step grammar rather than inventing a new one. Templates are DATA in src/templates.ts, served by GET /admin/templates, and read by BOTH the wizard preview and the launch path — so a template cannot preview one way and send another, which was the actual product bug in the previous shape. A third template is a new entry, not a code change; the founder can be told that in one sentence. Buttons resolve server-side from the registry by id and are never accepted from the request body, so the operator's freedom to edit the text cannot produce an arbitrary button title. Unknown templateId returns a real 400 instead of silently falling through to another template's buttons. The campaign marker carries the template id, so turn two knows which promise the opener made — the upsell asks who does the integration work instead of re-asking who they are, which is the difference between a follow-up and a contradiction.

grill.earned_clean_parts: Walked it as the operator on the live deploy at two viewports. The picker is a correct radiogroup — role=radiogroup, role=radio, tabindex=0, aria-checked tracking selection, Enter and Space both bound, and I confirmed the SPACE path flips state for real. Cards carry label, hint, «لِمن:» audience, and the template's actual buttons as chips, so the wrong opener is hard to pick by accident. The preview resolves {{1}} while the textarea correctly keeps the raw token — the right split, since one is what you edit and the other is what lands. Re-picking the active template restores its text, which is the escape hatch after an edit. tplLoad guards against overwriting text the operator typed in the first few hundred milliseconds. The launch button is genuinely disabled at zero targets rather than live-looking and dead. Zero console errors.

Twenty pixels above, the preview caption says «والملف يُرسَل عند طلبه». Two contradictory claims on one screen, at the moment of the send decision, and the wrong one is the one printed next to the launch button.

dashboard.ts:1156's empty-asset warning carries the same stale implication — «أضف الملف من معرفة الخدمة ليُضمَّن» tells the operator that adding an asset changes the opener's shape. It does not; it changes what arrives when the customer taps. Both strings are the same un-taught vocabulary (Rule 6, fifth corollary).

grill.earned_clean_parts: The seam is right and I want that on record: templates as data behind one endpoint read by both the preview and the wire is the correct boundary, and it eliminates a whole class of preview/send divergence. gupshup.ts remains the only file that knows the wire format. The rung-one guard was moved off process memory onto the transcript — correct, because there were 45 deploys in one day and an in-memory Set forgets. canonicalTitle's denylist→allowlist inversion is the right shape: it makes verb-form Arabic refusals impossible by construction rather than by enumeration, and I measured 0 of 14 named refusals inverting. The drop path prefers plain text over an unanswerable button, which is the correct failure direction. turnTextSends is per-phone, cleared at the top of each turn, and queue.ts serialises per key.

findings.finding: The system has the tap/typed provenance and throws it away. gupshup.ts parses msgType in BOTH webhook parsers and no consumer reads it; index.ts:44 drops it at the call site. Every intent lookup is therefore guessing from a string. This is not a missing feature — it is available data being discarded directly upstream of the decision that needs it, which is why one table addition could reach the ledger.

A new unguarded write path to a business outcome. agent.ts:830-833 calls setOutcome on any decline-matching text, and tracker.setOutcome overwrites unconditionally — unlike the turn-cap path at agent.ts:919, which explicitly guards `outcome !== 'handoff'`. A contact already at handoff or interested who taps «ليس الآن» on a proposed meeting time is silently downgraded, losing the chip the dashboard reads. Two defects in one branch: no provenance, and no state guard.

assertButtonsHandled() is one-directional — it checks emitted→has-intent, so ADDING a BUTTON_INTENT key is certified for free. The boot contract whose entire purpose is to stop unhandled button strings cannot see the change that caused this round's worst defect. A shared table with four consumers needs a consumer matrix, not a key list.

The allowlist is exact-string over the whole affix, so realistic compositions now refuse: «العرض التجاري، شكرًا» → undefined even though both «،» and «شكرًا» are individually benign; «الأحد صباحًا», «مكالمة قصيرة صباحًا», «أرسلوا لي الملف التعريفي» → all undefined (measured). Refusing is the SAFE direction and I am not asking for it to be loosened. But it means the scheduling close — the highest-value turn in the ladder — will frequently ship as plain text, and nothing measures how often. Instrument the drop rate before widening anything.

lostDecline at agent.ts:651-656 is dead by construction: dedupe keys on title and buttonIntent is a pure function of title, so any decline in options is necessarily in deduped. Exhaustively false. The comment claims «actually keep the decline this time» over code that never runs — the third round in a row a dedupe comment has claimed an action the code does not take. The real protection is the separate collapse-to-text guard.

grill.earned_clean_parts: Very little conventional slop, and the copy is the opposite of filler — the template hints, the «لِمن:» line, and the rung-one bodies are specific enough that a domain reader can tell them apart, which is the bar. The 400 messages are real Arabic sentences an operator can act on («القالب يحتوي {{1}} ولم تُحدَّد الخدمة — اختر الخدمة قبل الإطلاق»), not error codes. No purple gradients, no lorem, no dead buttons in the wizard, no TODO stubs. The example contact is honestly labelled «(مثال)». Comments explain WHY with measured detail rather than narrating the obvious.

findings.finding: FABRICATED DATA PRESENTED AS REAL — the canonical slop finding, in the ledger rather than the UI. «ضغط زر: لا» is written as the reason for an outcome when no button was pressed. This product's entire value proposition is that the AI's readings are grounded in what the customer actually did (Rule 4). A reason string that invents the customer's action is worse than an empty one.
«الملف مضمّن 📎» — a claim about what will be sent, printed next to the send button, that the send path contradicts.

TESTS THAT ASSERT NOTHING, three ways: four of five pixel comparisons are a file against itself (0.0000% arithmetically guaranteed); regression/build.log is 0 bytes and cited as exit_code 0 / verdict PASS; and the info-gate re-states the wantsInfo composition instead of executing it, so the reviewer's MUT5 flips && to || in the shipped predicate and all 133 assertions stay green. QA's own audit file names a fourth in its own gate: «CANNOT FAIL — the expectation is derived from the actual».

Two named measurement slots are shipped as empty objects: scenarios.cases[5].measured.unmappable_model_button_rejected = {} and concerns[0].measured['لا ترسلوا التفاصيل'] = {}. An empty object under a named assertion reads as coverage and is not.

scores.note: Intent fidelity is a 9 and it is the highest score this workstream has earned — he asked for a second template selectable at campaign creation with the value filled from the product, and that is exactly, demonstrably what exists on the live deploy; the registry shape even makes the third template free. It is not a 10 only because «let me test it» stops at the wire. Completeness is a 5 and it is what holds the verdict: there is no evidence bundle for the delivered commit, the deterministic gate is blocked, and a live defect corrupts the ledger the whole product exists to build. Evidence integrity is a 4 — the lowest score here — because the round's three loudest green numbers (0.0000% pixel diff, build PASS, 133/133) are each provably incapable of failing in the way that mattered. Taste holds at 8: the picker cards, the «لِمن:» line and the opener-aware turn two are genuinely good product thinking and should survive the rework verbatim.

change_orders.order: Gate every BUTTON_INTENT lookup on real tap provenance, then redeploy. The data already exists: gupshup.ts parses msgType in both webhook parsers and index.ts:44 discards it. Thread it through handleInbound and make buttonIntent() unreachable for typed text; treat unknown/absent msgType as TYPED, because mistaking a tap for typing only forgoes a shortcut while the reverse corrupts the ledger. Verify by executing the shipped source: typed «لا» must NOT reach the decline consumer and must NOT write an outcome; a real button-type «لا» must. NOTE: this is already sitting uncommitted in the worktree as isButtonTap() at gupshup.ts:174 wired at index.ts:46 — so the order is land it, review it, deploy it, and assert it. It is not done until the assertion exists and v186 is live.

Fix the outcome writer at agent.ts:830-833, not just its trigger. Two separate defects live in those four lines. (a) The reason string must state what actually happened — «ضغط زر: X» only when a tap is proven, otherwise the customer's own words, never an invented action. (b) Guard the overwrite the way the turn-cap path at agent.ts:919 already does: a contact at handoff or interested must not be silently downgraded to later by tapping «ليس الآن» on a meeting time. Also decide, explicitly, whether one «لا» should mean not_interested at all — the prompt at agent.ts:398 and :415 says to probe once and mark not-interested only «إذا تكرر الرفض», and the code contradicts its own prompt on the first tap.

Produce a delivery-evidence bundle bound to the DELIVERED commit and write it to the canonical path .orbit/qa/delivery-evidence.json, so that .orbit/checks/delivery-quality-gate.py --commit <sha> exits 0. Today that file is five commits stale at cb3fad0 and the round's real work sits in .orbit/artifacts/qa/ where the gate does not look. Three specific integrity requirements, each of which failed this round: every visual comparison must be against a baseline that is NOT byte-identical to its actual, or be reported as a re-baseline with no diff claim; a cited command's log must be non-empty and its exit code must come from the run, not the author (build.log is 0 bytes and cited as PASS); and a named `measured` slot must carry a value or the row is reported UNVERIFIED, never PASS. Resolve launch-path case G explicitly — verdict or UNVERIFIED, never silent, because it is an opt-out row.

Make the gate execute the shipped expression instead of restating it. The reviewer proved MUT5: flipping wantsInfo's composition from && to || in agent.ts leaves check-buttons at 133/133 green, because the gate slices the expression out and hand-types it back. Extract wantsInfo to a named exported function and import it. Then apply the same rule to every other assertion that reconstructs shipped logic — a gate that reconstructs a predicate is user-model Rule 7 by construction, and this one is now being quoted upward by three roles as proof.

Delete «الملف مضمّن 📎» from dashboard.ts:1171 and correct the sibling warning at :1156. The opener offers the file, it does not carry it; the preview caption on the same screen already says so. State what will actually be sent, next to the button that sends it. While there: either wire the buttons:false path to something an operator can choose, or delete the unreachable document-with-caption branch at index.ts:213 — a documented founder-facing trade-off that no real caller can select is a decision that exists only in a comment.

Give BUTTON_INTENT a consumer matrix and stop the class. The table has at least four readers — assertButtonsHandled, canonicalTitle, tappedCommercial, and the decline→setOutcome writer — and adding one key silently changes all four; that is precisely how «لا» reached the ledger past a boot contract designed to stop unhandled button strings. Assert, for every key, the behaviour of every consumer, generated from the table so a new key cannot be added without paying for its assertions. This is the structural exit from the thrashing ruled in §3, and it generalises round-24's hand-made disclosed/asked split instead of repeating it a third time.

Send the profile PDF and its value paragraph as ONE bubble on the rung-one path. agent.ts:868 calls gupshup.sendDocument without the caption argument that gupshup.ts:141 already accepts, so the customer who taps «تفاصيل التكامل» — this round's own button — gets a file with no words, then a separate paragraph. Round 25's ordering fix landed; the one-bubble requirement he stated in his own words did not.

Instrument the button drop rate before touching the allowlist again. «الأحد صباحًا», «مكالمة قصيرة صباحًا», «العرض التجاري، شكرًا» and «أرسلوا لي الملف التعريفي» all refuse today (measured), and each refusal ships the scheduling close as plain text. Refusing is the correct direction and must not be loosened on instinct — count it in production first, then decide with a number. The console.error already fires; aggregate it.

Give the sticky launch bar a compact state below ~430px so it stops covering the step-٣ template cards. He reviews on his phone and briefs by screenshot; the feature he asked for should not be the content the chrome hides.

Delete the dead lostDecline branch at agent.ts:651-656 or make it reachable. It is exhaustively false, and its comment claims an action the code does not take — the third consecutive round a dedupe comment has done that. A comment that describes unreachable code is a lie the next reviewer has to disprove by hand.

Capture one screenshot of the SECOND template selected, at 1440 and at 390, and keep it in the bundle. No image in the round shows the feature working, which is the single artifact he would accept as proof at a glance.

user_model_updates: 2026-08-13 R45/R46 round-26 [Rule 7 — the streak RESUMES after one clean round, and the channel is confirmed a third way]. Round-22 broke this rule's four-round streak by making instruments describe themselves. Round 26 resumes it in the same channel — the loop's PROSE about its evidence is unbounded by its evidence — and adds a third mechanism beyond over/under-claiming: an instrument that is STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE of the failure it is quoted for. Three at once, all measured: four of five pixel comparisons compare a file with itself (sha256-identical, so 0.0000% is arithmetic, not measurement); regression/build.log is 0 bytes and cited as exit_code 0 / verdict PASS; and MUT5 flips the shipped wantsInfo predicate from && to || with all 133 gate assertions still green, because the gate re-states the expression instead of executing it. The corollary to add: ask of every green number NOT «is it true» but «what input would make it red» — if the answer is «none», it is not evidence.

2026-08-13 R45/R46 round-26 [Rule 2 — FIRST EXTENSION FROM SCREENS TO THE LEDGER]. Every prior instance of «numbers must be real» was a rendered surface: a fabricated readiness card, invented knowledge scores, decorative 🔥 chips. This round the rule is violated in the DATABASE: agent.ts:832 writes «ضغط زر: لا» as the recorded reason for an outcome when the customer typed the word and pressed nothing. A false claim on a screen is corrected by a redeploy; a false claim in the ledger is permanent, propagates into every later reading, and is exactly the material Rule 4's causal explanations are built from. Rule 2 must be read as covering WRITES, not just renders. Watch for a second instance before promoting this to a numbered corollary.

2026-08-13 R45/R46 round-26 [THRASHING, second consecutive ruling, and the diagnosis sharpens]. Round 24 ruled thrashing on «one string answering two opposed questions» and named the exit: split disclosed from asked. That exit LANDED at round 25 and the shape reappeared within one round, one layer up (wantsInfo), then one layer above that (buttonIntent). The sharper diagnosis: the recurring unit is not a string, it is a SHARED TABLE OR MATCHER WITH MULTIPLE CONSUMERS, widened for one consumer and re-tested only for that consumer. Five commits, five new defects, one shape. The generalisable lesson: fixing one INSTANCE of a structural defect buys exactly one round; the fix has to make the property structural (a consumer matrix generated from the table) or the same class returns at a new address. Also new and important: severity went UP on the last step even as code footprint went DOWN — shrinking diffs are not evidence of convergence.

2026-08-13 R45/R46 round-26 [accepted pattern — DATA-SHAPED FEATURES ARE WHAT HE ASKED FOR, twice now]. He asked for «a second template»; what shipped was a registry where a third template is a new entry rather than a code change, served by one endpoint that both the preview and the send path read. This is the same shape that earned acceptance at round-22 (one numeral path, one catalogue). Signal 2 of 3 toward a rule: when he asks for «one more X», build the place where X lives, not the second X. Do NOT promote yet.

2026-08-13 R45/R46 round-26 [process, for the human ledger — deploy authorisation vs. definition of done]. «Once done, just deploy it and fly» (2026-08-10) was exercised five times in ninety minutes this round; four of those deploys carried an unreviewed new defect to production and the fifth is live with a known blocker. He pre-authorised the DEPLOY, not a redefinition of «done». Proposed loop amendment for human review via scripts/orbit-memory review: a commit that closes a reviewer blocker does not deploy until the reviewer has scored the commit that closes it. This is a playbook gap, not a builder failure — third round in which a fix shipped ahead of its own verification.
